title: Shortage of senior officers means rookies sometimes have to work alone, police say
article: City police say they have such a shortage of senior officers they are unable to implement a recommendation from a coroner's inquest that rookie officers not be partnered together.

"We try to deploy senior officers with less experienced officers as much as we can," Deputy Chief Jim Chu said Wednesday. "We try to do that. But sometimes officers that recently graduate from the police academy have to work alone or work with another partner."
The VPD has lost many of its senior officers through early retirement in recent years -- leaving many units with a large number of junior constables.

On Tuesday, a coroner's jury looking into the shooting death of Gerald Chenery recommended that officers with less than 18 months of combined experience should not be partners. Chenery was shot 12 times by constables Elizabeth Clark and Brian Smith, who had barely 31/2 months of policing experience between them.

Chu said Vancouver police will review all the jury's recommendations and decide whether to make any changes in the next few weeks. But Chu stressed an investigation by the force found Clark and Smith acted appropriately.

"These officers acted with great bravery and in accordance with their training and the law," said Chu. "The fact that they were junior is not an issue in this case. Senior officers would have acted similarly."

The officers encountered Chenery on Dec. 26, 2004, while on patrol on East Hastings. When Chenery seemed to try to avoid the officers, he was questioned, and they learned he was wanted on a warrant from a parole office but that the warrant should not be executed until an officer phoned.

Chenery pulled two knives and charged Clark, who fired four shots, hitting Chenery once. Smith, who testified he thought his partner was being stabbed and that her life was in danger, shot Chenery 11 times.
